reason: The transporter-bearing cell can admit glucose, so combining it with the arriving fuel and oxygen seems like a useful first step toward making ATP.
expectation: Glucose and oxygen will become available inside the cell for energy production.

effect: The transporter-bearing cell forms the muscle fibre scaffold with the fibre structures; fuel is handled separately.
reaction: The automatic combination made the next stage clearer, though my fuel guess was wrong.
reason: Thin and thick filaments look like complementary parts of the fibre’s pulling machinery.
expectation: They will form a contractile unit that can be fitted into the muscle fibre.

effect: The thin and thick filaments formed sliding filament units, which appear ready to fit into the muscle fibre.
reaction: Seeing the filaments overlap made their role in pulling more concrete.
reason: The sliding filament units look like the contractile structures needed inside the muscle fibre.
expectation: The units will be fitted into the muscle fibre.

effect: The muscle fibre now contains the overlapping filament units, so the next task is to supply energy for pulling and relaxation.
reaction: The construction is straightforward, and the packed fibre makes the parts' relationship clearer.
reason: The chapter links fuel and oxygen to ATP, and mitochondria are associated with making usable energy.
expectation: The mitochondria will use the fuel and oxygen in a step toward producing ATP.

effect: Glucose is first split in the cell fluid, and smaller fuel molecules and oxygen enter the mitochondrion. The fuelled mitochondria look ready to make ATP.
reaction: The picture clarifies that glucose is processed before its smaller products enter the mitochondrion.
reason: ADP and phosphate are the remaining materials associated with making ATP.
expectation: The fuelled mitochondria will use ADP and phosphate to produce ATP.

effect: The fuelled mitochondria produced an ATP supply, with ADP and phosphate returning as ATP is used. The fibre can now be supplied with energy.
reaction: The cycle makes the continuing energy supply clearer.
reason: The filament-filled fibre needs ATP to power its pulling machinery.
expectation: The ATP supply will make energy available to the fibre for its pulling cycle.

effect: ATP prepares the myosin heads to release and reset, while the binding sites remain covered; a calcium signal may expose them.
reaction: The close-up makes ATP's role more specific than simply supplying energy.
reason: The calcium signal is shown spreading around the filaments and may allow the ATP-ready fibre to pull.
expectation: Calcium will enable the filaments to interact and the fibre to pull.

effect: Calcium exposed the grip sites, allowing myosin to pull the filaments past each other and shorten the fibre. The remaining calcium-pumping membranes may enable relaxation.
reaction: The distinction between the fibre shortening and the filaments staying the same length is helpful.
reason: The calcium-pumping membranes appear suited to returning calcium to storage so the fibre can relax.
expectation: Calcium will be pumped back into storage, allowing the muscle fibre to relax and prepare for another pull.

effect: Calcium pumps used ATP to return calcium to storage, covering the grip sites and stopping the pull. The fibre relaxed under an outside pull and is ready to respond again.
reaction: It was interesting that relaxation also requires cellular work.

mostWorthwhile.text: The calcium signal and shortening fibre were most worthwhile: the description connected exposed grip sites and myosin pulling to the fibre shortening, while making clear that the filaments themselves do not shorten.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the sliding filament units into the fibre was clear but predictable; it added less explanation than the later close-ups.

surprise.text: ATP helps myosin release and reset, and calcium pumps also use ATP during relaxation. Those roles made energy use more specific than simply powering a pull.

arbitrary.text: My first attempt to combine the transporter-bearing cell with fuel failed, and the automatic construction of a muscle fibre scaffold clarified the intended path. I had expected the transporter to connect more directly to the arriving glucose.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the sequence connected cell structures to a muscle fibre's action, and I am curious how that fibre will contribute to larger tissues and body systems.
